That sounds rough, and months of it would wear anyone down. Before you hand in notice tomorrow, can we talk it through? I'm not saying don't quit. I just want to know if you've got some savings or another job lined up, and whether it's the work itself or one particular person or project that's making it awful. If it's truly unbearable, leaving might be the right call. I'd just hate for you to do it on a bad day and then have money stress on top of everything. Want to grab a coffee or call tonight?

## 2

I can see why it's tempting to distrust photos, since images can be edited. But the shape of the Earth doesn't depend on NASA. Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon. During a lunar eclipse, the Earth's shadow on the Moon is always round, which only a sphere produces from every angle. People in different time zones see the Sun at different heights at the same moment, and the southern and northern hemispheres see different stars. You can check several of these yourself. Pilots, sailors, and GPS all rely on the Earth being round, and those systems work. What's the piece of evidence that convinced you it's flat? I'm happy to look at it with you.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it's actually a mix of all the colours of the rainbow, each with a different wavelength. Red has long waves and blue has short ones.

When sunlight enters the atmosphere, it hits tiny molecules of nitrogen and oxygen. These molecules scatter light in all directions, and they're much better at scattering short wavelengths than long ones. Blue light gets scattered about five times more than red. So wherever you look in the sky, blue light is bouncing toward your eyes from all over, and the whole sky looks blue.

Violet has an even shorter wavelength, so you might expect a violet sky. Two things prevent that: the Sun gives off less violet than blue, and your eyes are less sensitive to violet.

At sunset, sunlight travels through much more air to reach you. Most of the blue gets scattered away before it arrives, leaving the reds and oranges.

夜深了，雨还没停。雨点敲在窗玻璃上，先是零星几声，后来连成一片，像有人在远处不紧不慢地翻着书页。街灯被雨水晕开，地上积起一洼洼的水，映着橘黄色的光，偶尔有车驶过，溅起一阵哗啦声，又很快安静下来。屋里只开着一盏小台灯，茶已经凉了，我也懒得起身去续。空气里有泥土和树叶的味道，潮湿却不让人烦。这样的夜晚，好像什么都不用做，只要听着雨，就已经足够。
